findings.diagnosis: The scorer underestimates entailment (contra) risk for cuts that leave a very short trailing fragment. It treats locally-cohesive left/right translations as safe even when the right-hand fragment, taken alone, would assert/negate or mis‑scope a claim and so overturn the earlier material.
findings.evidence: ids: ["en_us_1567","en_us_738","en_us_655","en_us_936","en_us_1527","en_us_1617","en_us_46","en_us_845","en_us_538","en_us_733","en_us_1428"] — each policy kept a cut that isolates a short (1–3 word) trailing span (names, locations, prepositional heads, or bare nouns/numerals) whose standalone meaning contradicts or inverts the preceding text, causing the set to fail.

edit.text: If the right-hand fragment is very short (≤3 words) or is a bare name/location/measure/preposition, ask: 'Could this fragment alone assert or invert the left-hand claim?' If yes, mark the cut as high contra-risk and rank it low.
